headline: Xpeng says it hopes to start testing its Yoyo driverless taxis in selected cities outside China next year, with wider rollout possible in two to three years.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a first-hand interview with a senior executive adds the overseas timetable, but it is a plan with no named cities or partners.
importance_line: Riders and rival robotaxi firms outside China may see Xpeng's driverless taxis within a few years, but the cities, partners and rules are unnamed and the timetable is an executive's hope, not a commitment.
summary: CNA reports, from an interview with Xpeng vice-chairman and president Brian Gu in Singapore, that the Chinese car maker hopes to begin pilot testing of its Yoyo robotaxis in selected cities outside China next year, without naming them, and that larger-scale commercial use around the world could follow two to three years later. This continues our 9 Oct 2026 entry on Yoyo's invitation-only trials: the new details are that close to 100 vehicles are in the Guangzhou pilot and that Xpeng's Iron humanoid robot will work in its own stores before being offered to outside customers in the second half of 2027.
notes: Interview is dated 9 Oct 2026; flagged as a follow-up of the Yoyo story carried on 9 Oct 2026.
